name: Scrapgospel Pilgrim's Patchwork Shroud
description:
A full-length outer garment assembled from at least forty distinct fabric salvages — factory floor insulation, transit seat upholstery, synthetic fur scraps, acid-bleached cargo tarp — stitched together in a deliberate mandala pattern centered on the back. Practitioners of the Shelf-born Meridian Drift faith wear this as both devotional garment and survival layer. Embroidered circuit diagrams intersperse with hand-painted deity glyphs drawn from a syncretized mix of Yoruba, Shinto, and Orthodox iconography, all reinterpreted through a post-corporate lens.

Each shroud is unique, assembled over years, and added to after significant life events. The hem drags deliberately — a statement that the wearer is not running from anything.
functionality: Layered construction provides genuine thermal insulation against Shelf acid rain. The outer tarp-fabric layer repels light chemical exposure. Deep interior pockets are sewn into the lining at devotional intervals — each holds a small sacred object.
what_it_says: This person carries their entire spiritual history on their back and answers to no corponation's calendar.
worn_by: DIY anti-corporate artists using faith as framework
story_hooks: A shroud surfaces at a Tier 4 auction house — someone sold a dead elder's devotional garment, and the community wants it back.
One of the embroidered circuit diagrams is a functional schematic for something that shouldn't exist on the Shelf.
A new Meridian Drift convert is being pressured to burn their shroud as proof of corporate loyalty — they refuse.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length, flowing outer robe with a deliberately asymmetrical silhouette. The garment reads as both sacred vestment and survival armor—a walking collage of industrial salvage unified by intricate hand-stitching. The back features a hypnotic mandala pattern that draws the eye downward, while the front presents a chaotic-harmonious patchwork of contrasting textures and hues. Worn by practitioners of Shelf-born Meridian Drift, it announces spiritual devotion and urban-scavenger heritage simultaneously.
physical_description.fit: Loose, flowing, and deliberately voluminous—designed for layering over augmented frames and protective gear. The cut prioritizes movement and accommodation of diverse body modifications. Sleeves are generously tapered; the hem drags 2-3 inches past the ankle, a conscious choice signaling rootedness rather than haste.
physical_description.primary_material: Composite salvage: factory insulation felt, transit seat upholstery (dense synthetic), acid-treated cargo tarp (reinforced weave), synthetic fur scraps, recycled textile composites. Each patch varies in weight and durability—a functional archive of urban waste streams.
physical_description.texture: Deliberately mixed and tactile. Sections are quilted, others smooth; some rough-textured insulation contrasts against slick tarp material. Embroidered circuit diagrams create raised linear texture across chest and sleeves. Hand-painted deity glyphs sit matte atop glossier patches. Overall impression: built rather than manufactured.
physical_description.color_scheme: A deliberately chaotic spectrum—grays, blacks, and browns from industrial salvage form the base. Accent colors emerge from original upholstery: deep teal, rust orange, faded crimson. Gold and copper thread in embroidery. Acid-bleached patches create pale yellow and white negative space. The mandala on the back uses symmetrical color blocking to anchor the visual chaos.
physical_description.closures: None—the shroud is designed to be drawn over the body and allowed to drape naturally. Some versions feature optional linen ties at the shoulders for ceremonial occasions, but these are non-functional.
distinctive_features: Back mandala pattern: concentric circles of stitched fabric radiating from a central glyph representing the Meridian Drift cosmology
Embroidered circuit diagrams mimicking neural pathways, interspersed with hand-painted deity glyphs (syncretic Yoruba-Shinto-Orthodox fusion)
Deliberately dragging hem—no hemming tape, edges deliberately frayed and raw
Visible mending and patching from 'life event' additions—each section dated informally with faded ink
Reinforced panels at shoulders and back (thicker insulation) for durability
Hidden inner pockets (salvaged cargo tarp pockets remain functional)
No brand markers—maker's initials sometimes stitched into hem in tiny, humble script
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Sub-grade aesthetic reclaimed as devotional. The poverty-adjacent materials signal economic precarity, but the labor investment and spiritual intentionality elevate it beyond mere survival wear. Practices deliberate anti-wealth signaling.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf-born Meridian Drift practitioners—a syncretic spiritual movement among GLMZ sub-grade and working-class communities (Tiers 3-5). Signals rejection of corpo-spiritual commodification, embrace of salvage ethics, and deep community rootedness. The garment is a living archive: each patch represents a crisis survived, a prayer answered, a year completed.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always visibly worn, never pristine. Patina is intentional and honored. Fresh additions are visible—newer patches slightly cleaner, embroidery still sharp. Older sections show weathering, thread-fade, and careful repair. The garment ages publicly and communally.
